events.title: Birth of John Calvin
events.description: John Calvin, the French theologian and reformer, was born in Noyon, Picardy. He later became a leading figure of the Protestant Reformation and based his ministry in Geneva.
events.significance: Calvin's writings, especially the Institutes of the Christian Religion, founded Calvinism and Reformed Christianity, which shaped religious, political, and social life across Europe and North America.

events.title: Lady Jane Grey Proclaimed Queen of England
events.description: Following the death of Edward VI on July 6, Lady Jane Grey was proclaimed Queen of England and taken to the Tower of London, in accordance with Edward's plan to keep the throne Protestant.
events.significance: Her reign lasted only about nine days before Mary I gained popular support and took the throne, making it one of the shortest and most dramatic succession crises in English history.

events.title: Wyoming Admitted as the 44th U.S. State
events.description: President Benjamin Harrison signed the act admitting Wyoming to the Union as the 44th state. Wyoming had already granted women the right to vote in 1869 as a territory.
events.significance: Wyoming became the first state to enter the Union with full woman suffrage, earning the nickname the Equality State and advancing the women's rights movement.

events.title: Scopes Trial Begins in Dayton, Tennessee
events.description: The trial of high school teacher John T. Scopes began on charges of violating Tennessee's Butler Act by teaching human evolution. The case featured Clarence Darrow for the defense and William Jennings Bryan for the prosecution.
events.significance: The 'Monkey Trial' became a landmark cultural clash between science and religious fundamentalism, and it drew national media attention to the debate over teaching evolution in public schools.

events.title: Battle of Britain Begins
events.description: German forces began major air attacks on British shipping convoys in the English Channel and on ports, which is commonly regarded as the start of the Battle of Britain.
events.significance: The Royal Air Force's defense prevented a German air superiority victory and thwarted plans for invasion, marking Hitler's first major setback in World War II.
